messages:
Marina CSM: Quick check-in on AcmeCorp onboarding — noticed their p95 token latency jumped yesterday from ~420ms -> ~1.2s on the hosted route. Thinking we should propose an int8 pilot on a subset of traffic, plus route pin to us-east and a prefix-cache tweak. @Sanjay @Oliver any blockers?
Sanjay (SE): can you paste the traces? any pattern in seq_len or model churn?
Marina CSM: pasted a small tail of traces below (sanitized):
```
2025-03-15T18:22:11Z route=/api/v1/generate p95=1200ms seq_len=512 tokens_out=64 model=redwood-medium-fp16
2025-03-15T18:22:12Z route=/api/v1/generate p95=430ms seq_len=128 tokens_out=12 model=redwood-medium-fp16
2025-03-15T18:23:05Z route=/api/v1/generate p95=1150ms seq_len=600 tokens_out=80 model=redwood-medium-fp16
```
Sanjay (SE): pattern: long-sequence batches correlate with spikes. Int8 quant can reduce per-token GPU latency ~20-30% for these lengths, but expect a small quality delta. Routing-wise: do a 30% canary to int8 in us-east, with automatic fallback to fp16 on quality/errors. Also enable prefix caching for repeated system prompts (TTL ~60s).
Oliver (ML): Candidate variant: `redwood-medium-int8-2025-03`. We need Acme's onboarding prompt set to run a micro-eval (100-500 prompts) and check BLEU/F1/semantic-similarity. Also confirm KV-cache compatibility (int8 path reuses same kv layout). If we can't run their exact prompts, we can sample from similar workloads.
Bob - AcmeOps: we can approve a small canary. Concern: customer-visible regressions — we need rollback safety and clear SLOs. Also any impact on determinism for caching?
Oliver (ML): Determinism: tiny surface diffs expected, not behavioural shifts. We'll set pass/fail thresholds: if semantic similarity <98% or QA F1 drops >2% we rollback. Caching should operate the same since prompt normalization unchanged.
Marina CSM: FYI renewal note — Acme is on a 6mo renewal; they flagged perf regressions in the last health check. Proactively executing this canary + enablement session should reduce churn risk. I'll book a 30-min customer call for consent.
Sanjay (SE): Draft rollout plan (high level):
- Step 1: build variant `redwood-medium-int8-2025-03` and run internal micro-eval
- Step 2: stage canary: route 30% traffic `acme-route -> int8` (weighting)
- Step 3: enable prefix cache TTL=60s and small KV prefetch for repeated system prompts
- Step 4: monitoring/guardrails: p50/p95, token cost, 5xx rate; auto-rollback if 5xx > 0.5% or p95 regresses beyond baseline+20%
- Step 5: escalate to 60% after 24h if metrics stable
I'll attach a deployment snippet: 
```bash
# canary weight update (example)
rictl routes update acme-route --add-variant redwood-medium-int8-2025-03 --set-weight redwood-medium-int8-2025-03=30
```
Marina CSM: @deploy-bot kick the canary when ready. I'll message Acme with the plan and the rollback criteria.
deploy-bot: Canary queued: acme-route -> redwood-medium-int8-2025-03 (canary id cj-7751). Logs will stream to #eng-releases and will notify on anomalies.
Bob - AcmeOps: thanks — ETA? our internal release window opens Monday.
Sanjay (SE): aiming to start canary within 2 business hours. We'll run 1k synthetic requests derived from onboarding prompts in staging to validate metrics, then start the live 30% canary. Will post the micro-eval results here.
Oliver (ML): I'll run the paired A/B micro-eval and post diffs (semantic sim, QA F1, latency, token-cost). If diffs are within thresholds we signal proceed. If not, rollback and propose alternate: dynamic routing by request-length to prefer fp16 for seq_len>512.
Marina CSM: Perfect. I'll capture action items and update the renewal playbook and customer health dashboard. Thanks team :sparkles:
